main_concerns.concern: All seven evidence items are meta-artifacts (contracts, claims, receipts, evidence summaries) — none provides runtime proof that the probes detect real provider disagreement. The evidence chain is self-referential: RSP evidence validates the RSP claim which references RSP receipts generated by the same tooling that produced the claim. This is a closeout-artifact stack, not implementation verification.

The evidence is structural and self-referential. Generated receipts from the same runtime under review do not prove that provider disagreement is now explicitly surfaced, bounded, and executable at decision time. The main claim conflates 'files were added' with 'RedCap no longer blindly obeys or silently dismisses Prism providers.'

minimum_fixes.minimum_fix: Provide a single execution transcript where a positive consensus check passes because two providers genuinely agreed AND a negative probe fails because two providers genuinely disagreed on the same review — with the raw provider outputs included, not just the consensus wrapper's summary.

Provide one runtime scenario trace (or integration test log) showing conflicting Kimi/Claude Code reviews and the new logic producing an explicit, bounded, executable outcome instead of blind obedience or silent dismissal. Also show that removing the guard makes the negative probe fail for the intended reason.
